arthurian.text: Welcome to Tintagel! Were Arthur and Merlin here? It's a poet's tale, a medieval storyteller's tale, and the tourist board's mission statement.
The real castle was built in the 1230s by Richard, Earl of Cornwall. He wanted a famous place. He got one.

postmaster.text: This house is from the 1380s. It was a farmhouse, and from 1844 to 1892 it was a post office. The roof sags like a hammock.
It's now owned by the National Trust. The roof is also owned by the National Trust. The sag, I think, was a gift.

pasty_seller.text: A proper Cornish pasty has a crimped edge, shaped like a D, with beef, potato, swede and onion. No carrots. Never carrots.
Pasties have PGI status, like Melton Mowbray pork pies. If it isn't made in Cornwall, it's only a pasty-shaped wrap.

kernow_fan.text: Dydh da! That's 'good day' in Cornish, Kernewek. We've been bringing it back, a bit at a time.
Kernow is Cornwall. One and All, 'Onen hag Oll', is the motto. It's on every shirt. It's even on my pasty bag.

then.text: I am regrouping. Penzance next. The mine, you know. Do not follow me. I mean it. Do follow me. No. Don't.

else.text: Merlin's Cave! Look at the echo. We'll sell the echo. 'The Echo Experience'. First tier gets one echo, second tier gets two.
Ah, the young walker. Tintagel, splendid, isn't it? We're thinking a gift shop in the castle. Perhaps a zip line to Merlin's cave.
Regional Director, England. Pryce spoke of you. Briefly, and with a twitch.
Hrmph. I shall retire to Penzance, where the mine is. The tin, you see. Very old, very valuable, and sleeping badly.
Dydh da, as they say here. I am told that is 'good day'. It is, I'm told, a good day. For somebody.
He tips his Panama, flicks a smear of sea spray off his blazer, and sweeps off down the cliff path towards the Penzance road.

gate_tintagel.text: Road to Penzance closed. Sir Rupert Ashcombe's orders. He likes to meet people properly first.
He's in Merlin's Cave, up the cliff path, at the west end of town. Dress code: smart casual. Hard hat, optional.
